limitations: one policy (random) and one field (uniform); a biased draw would be visible here but the cause of the bias would not
the 0.625 of EXP-41 came from 24 choices on one organism; this run uses 50000, so it can only say the draw is not biased, not why EXP-41 was low
the silent control uses remember and stay, not a second random run: it checks that the counter can read both ends, not that the draw is unbiased
organisms die during the run, so later frames contribute fewer choices; the count is over living samples only
the decision is read from `direction`, which EXP-44 showed is the decision of the frame it appears in, not of the next step
